points.text: Related work omits input-format sensitivity literature; 'unexplored' framing overstated.
Novelty modest relative to structure-aware parsers and markup-preserving prior work.
No baseline with structure-preserving parser or non-LaTeX serialization.
Premise that OCR text degrades performance contradicted by Table 1.
Cited works do not clearly support premise; ColBERT citation misused.
Attention treated as causal without discussing sink tokens or faithfulness literature.
Gains reported over image-only; versus image+OCR they largely vanish.
'Best results on almost every dataset' overstated; best in 10 of 16.
Structured text confounded with extra MLLM pass; no equal-pass controls.
Generator MLLM, prompt and extra cost not reported.
Structured-only worse than OCR-only for all models, contradicting thesis.
Single run; no seeds, CIs or test sizes.
LLM judge not validated against human labels or benchmark metrics.
Open/closed-domain settings and baseline provenance unclear.
No causal intervention supports 'structured attention is key'.
Attention analysis: one model, unclear selection, no OCR condition, token-count confound.
Table 3 numbers inconsistent with Tables 1-2.
Element-type claim (charts/tables gain more) not supported by Table 3.
Table 2 caption and 'ans' typo.
Limitations section lists open questions, not method limitations.
Arithmetic errors in Table 1 and Table 3 averages, text-table mismatch.
'10% improvement' misstates the gain.
Claims and observations asserted more strongly than evidence supports.
Image+OCR comparison buried; headline gains from weak image-only baselines.
Missing prompts, generator, decoding, sample counts and code.
Limitations section consists of questions.
Caption, typo, '10%' wording, unreadable Figure 6 labels.
Cost of extra per-page MLLM generation not reported.
Assumes gold evidence pages; no end-to-end retrieval run.
Error and hallucination rate of generated LaTeX not reported.
Evaluated only on 7B models.
Assumes attention distribution explains behavior; no intervention.
Alternative structure formats (Markdown, JSON, accessibility trees) untested.
Noisy-OCR domains (scanned, handwritten, non-English) untested.
Limitations and broader-impact discussion almost absent.
No failure-case analysis.
Versus image+OCR control, gains small or negative; thesis not supported.
Structured-only below OCR-only for all models.
Format confounded with extra MLLM processing.
'OCR often degrades' holds in only 2 of 16 cells.
Causal reading of attention without intervention.
Attention analysis single model, no OCR condition, token-count confound, unexplained selection.
'Almost best' claim overstated (10/16).
Single run without CIs; tiny differences.
Binary LLM judge unvalidated.
Sample sizes, settings and baseline provenance unstated.
Table 3 does not reconcile with Tables 1-2.
Element-type claim unsupported.
Arithmetic and consistency slips in tables.
'10% improvement' wording.
Table 2 caption says 'different datasets' for two.
Incremental novelty; structure-preserving markup is not new; LaTeX a thin tweak.
No principled justification for LaTeX over simpler structured formats.
Observations 1-3 are mostly empirical restatements.
Generator MLLM, prompts and settings unspecified.
Stronger generator model could make gains unfair.
No latency, token or cost accounting.
Missing stronger structured-evidence baselines (HTML/Markdown, doc-structure tools).
Attention analysis over-interpreted; no causal link.
Table 3 shows degraded performance on some subsets; inconsistent gains.
Observation that plain OCR text hurts is not novel.
Method is prompt engineering without technical novelty.
Only 7B open models; no larger or proprietary models.
MLLM-based LaTeX generation error-prone and not scalable for real documents.
No comparison with HTML, XML or Markdown formats.
LaTeX may not encode irregular layouts or handwritten annotations.
Structured text alone performs poorly; method requires image input.
Effect of OCR errors on structured text not discussed.
Only 7B models; scale dependence unexplored.
Main conclusion too simple for top-tier venue.
Token-count differences from resolution or formatting not controlled.
Attention analysis shallow.
Figure 4 attention scores unnormalized; left comparison unclear.

P.summary: Related work omits input-format sensitivity literature.
Modest novelty versus structure-aware parsers and markup work.
No alternative structure-format or parser baselines.
Observation 1 (OCR hurts) contradicted by own results.
Attention treated as causal without intervention.
Attention analysis setup lacks OCR condition and token-count control.
Gains measured against image-only; small or negative versus image+OCR.
Structure confounded with extra MLLM generation pass.
Settings, sample sizes and baseline provenance unclear.

Q.summary: Method novelty incremental; prompt engineering; too simple.
No comparison or justification versus other structured formats.
Table 3 shows inconsistent gains across subsets.
MLLM LaTeX generation error-prone and unscalable.
